---
title: "How to write a post (this file never publishes)"
date: 2000-01-01
---

The leading underscore in the filename keeps this out of the blog listing and
out of the rendered site. It is a reference file, not a post.

## Adding a post

Create a `.qmd` file in this folder. It needs two fields:

``` yaml
---
title: "Your post title"
date: 2026-08-05
description: "One line that shows up in the listing."
categories: [breeding informatics, nanopore]
---

Body in Markdown.
```

That is the whole workflow. The blog page picks it up, sorts by date,
generates the RSS feed, and turns `categories` into filter buttons. The three
most recent posts also appear on the home page.

Filenames do not matter — dating them just keeps the folder readable. Posts
with no R code can be saved as `.md` and render faster. Shared defaults
(author, date format) live in `_metadata.yml` next to this file.

## Running code in a post

``` {{r}}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6
plot(pressure)
```

The figure is computed at render time and baked into the HTML, so the
published site stays static.

## Useful bits

A shaded callout:

``` markdown
::: {.panel}
**Heads up.** Text goes here.
:::
```

The accent underline: `[phrase]{.accent}`.
